mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the preceding month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market softness reduces growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: early signs of labor market weakening before recession
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day ahead returns show no significant correlation with the combined labor-inflation signal (Rank IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% from the prior month's level coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO rising >2% (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) over two consecutive months triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects weakening supply constraints.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both decline in consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the two-month supply decline pattern is absent (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates continued accommodative policy.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when UNRATE remains below 4% for the next 3 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual, we use a rising RSAFS as a labor absorption proxy) combined with a decline in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to wage pressure and inflation fears.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market tightening with deflationary pressures
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative when the labor absorption-inflation cross is absent (Rank IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.5% and FEDFUNDS remains below 4%, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 20-day forward return as the market anticipates future rate stability and inflationary easing.
regime_hint: moderate inflation with low policy rate
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the inflation-rate and policy conditions are not met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer demand measured by a decline in GDPC1 of over 5% in a month leads to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals demand destruction and reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 does not fall by >5% (p > 0.05).
